sections.plantingGuide:
Site Selection
Use well-drained, deep loamy soil that is not stony or gravelly. Cassava can also thrive in poor
or marginal soils. It requires full sun, rainfall of 150-200 cm (or about 6 months of rain per year),
and a temperature range of 21-35°C.

Seed Rate
Use about 50 bundles of 1 m stem cuttings per hectare, giving approximately 10,000 stands/ha
at 1 m x 1 m spacing. Erect varieties such as TME 419 can be spaced at 100 cm x 75 cm for a
higher plant population.

Spacing
Standard spacing: 1 m x 1 m on flats, ridges or mounds.
Erect varieties: 100 cm x 75 cm.

Planting Method
Cassava is propagated by stem cuttings. Plant approximately 25 cm-long stems with 4-6 nodes
at about 30 cm depth. The supplied source further states: dip cuttings in chlorpyrifos solution (2
ml/1 L water) for 5 minutes before planting; apply glyphosate at 4-5 L/ha 10 days before
cultivation, or apply pre-emergence herbicide (Primextra) at 5 L/ha within 3 days after planting.
Application caution: Agrochemical use should follow current product labels, registration status
and applicable safety guidance.
sections.harvestStorage:
Harvesting
Maturity indicators: 8-12 months after planting, depending on variety and location.

Manual method: Hand pulling and digging using a hoe, cutlass or spade after cutting the
stems.
Mechanical method: Harvesters uproot the tuberous roots, which are then picked by hand.
Expected yield: 16-53 t/ha fresh root yield depending on variety. Examples stated in the
source: TMS 90257 - 43 t/ha; TMS 98/002 - 48.4 t/ha; Umucass 43 - 53 t/ha.

Storage
Cover harvested cassava roots with jute bags and sprinkle water to keep them moist. Store for a
maximum of 2-4 days before processing because cassava deteriorates rapidly after harvest.
